newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia coal export earnings to rise-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia coal export earnings to rise-ABARE.

text.p: Australia's coal export earnings are forecast to rise 2.4 percent in 1996/97 in line with a rise in both the volume of exports and average prices, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.
In its December quarter Commodities bulletin, ABARE forecast export earnings of A$7.94 billion in the year to June 30, 1997, up from A$7.76 billion in 1995/96.
However, ABARE has revised down its export earnings forecast from the A$8.24 billion it predicted in its September quarter bulletin because of the expected strength in the Australian dollar.

It said it now expected Australian coal exports to rise 5.1 percent to 145.7 million tonnes in 1996/97, while total coal production was also forecast to recover, rising 3.9 percent to 202.2 million tonnes.
Tightening world supply of metallurgical coal in an environment of expanding global demand was expected to result in an increase in prices, particularly for hard coking coal.
"The outlook for metallurgical coal prices is influenced by the likelihood of a consolidation of growth in world steel production over the next year, requiring additional coal supplies," ABARE said.
It said Taiwan would lead this growth, while India's crude steel production was also forecast to expand significantly.
Slight growth was also forecast for Australia's major metallurgical coal market, Japan, with Australia's share of exports there expected to rise to 50 percent, it said.
Thermal coal demand was also forecast to increase modestly in 1996/97 as Asian markets expand coal fired electricity generation capacity, ABARE said.
